advances:
The endpoint first-moment coefficient cannot collapse in a compact
genuine-fan gauge.  There is a canonical pair of points, one in each
midpoint body from
\(P_\varnothing\times Q_1\) and
\(P_\varnothing\times Q_2\), whose transverse separation \(B_U\)
satisfies an explicit positive lower bound depending only on the
compact-gauge constants.

The proof uses the first and second crossings through the canonical
left tails.  It does not use a lower bound depending only on
\(p_\varnothing,q_1,q_2\).  In normalized fan coordinates the endpoint
offset defect first gives
\[
B_U>
\frac{\eta+(q_1+q_2)g/(2D)}{H},
\]
where \(\eta>6d\), \(D\) bounds the diameter of \(A_2\),
\(g=\min(\|\nabla\psi_1\|,\|\nabla\psi_2\|)\), and
\(H=\|\nabla(\psi_1-\psi_2)\|\).  The crossings, tails, and no-half
inequality then force
\[
C B_U^2+A B_U>\frac1{13},
\qquad
C=\frac{H^2}{2|\det(\nabla\psi_1,\nabla\psi_2)|},
\qquad
A=\frac{2DH}{g}.
\]
Thus \(B_U\) has a positive zeroth-order modulus.  In particular, a
putative collapse \(B_U(d)=\beta_Ud+o(d)\) is impossible under the
full scalar hypotheses; even without those hypotheses, the offset
condition alone gives
\(\liminf B_U(d)/d\geq6/H_0\).

Consequently, once a separate finite-stage estimate
\(\Delta_3\geq cB_U-Ed\) is available, the exact third crossing
\(\Delta_3=0\) is contradicted for all sufficiently small \(d\).
This packet supplies the endpoint first-moment half of that argument,
not the third-crossing stability estimate.

proof:
The normalization (4) is an exact parameterization of the paired
endpoint cuts.  Set
\[
a_i=3d\left(L_i+\frac13\right),
\qquad
b_i=3d\left(\frac13-L_i\right)=2d-a_i.
\tag{16}
\]
Then
\[
P_J
=A_0\cap
\{\psi_i\leq a_i\ (i\in J),\
  \psi_i>a_i\ (i\notin J)\},
\]
\[
Q_J
=A_2\cap
\{\psi_i\leq b_i\ (i\in J),\
  \psi_i>b_i\ (i\notin J)\}.
\tag{17}
\]
The offset hypothesis in accepted fact `0e51a47a9add571f` gives
\[
\sum_i a_i=3d\left(\sum_iL_i+1\right)<0.
\tag{18}
\]
Consequently, if
\[
\delta=-\sum_i a_i,\qquad
\eta=\sum_i b_i,
\]
then
\[
\delta>0,\qquad
\eta=6d+\delta>6d.
\tag{19}
\]

We first estimate the transverse first moments of \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\).
For \(y\in Q_1\), write
\[
\alpha=b_1-\psi_1(y)\geq0,\qquad
\sigma=\psi_2(y)-b_2>0.
\]
Using (5),
\[
\psi_3(y)-b_3
=\alpha-\sigma-\eta>0,
\]
and hence
\[
\alpha>\eta+\sigma.
\tag{20}
\]
It follows that
\[
(\psi_1-\psi_2)(y)
=b_1-b_2-\alpha-\sigma
<b_1-b_2-\eta-2\sigma.
\tag{21}
\]
Similarly, for \(y\in Q_2\), write
\[
\rho=\psi_1(y)-b_1>0,\qquad
\gamma=b_2-\psi_2(y)\geq0.
\]
The inequality \(\psi_3(y)>b_3\) gives
\[
\gamma>\eta+\rho,
\]
and therefore
\[
(\psi_1-\psi_2)(y)
>b_1-b_2+\eta+2\rho.
\tag{22}
\]

Let
\[
\overline\sigma
=\frac1{q_1}\int_{Q_1}(\psi_2-b_2),
\qquad
\overline\rho
=\frac1{q_2}\int_{Q_2}(\psi_1-b_1).
\tag{23}
\]
Averaging (21)-(22), using (8), and cancelling the common
\(x_\varnothing\) term gives
\[
B_U>
\frac{\eta+\overline\sigma+\overline\rho}{H}.
\tag{24}
\]

The two mean slacks have exact area lower bounds.  We prove the first;
the second is identical.  Slice \(Q_1\) by the signed-distance
coordinate
\[
r=\frac{\psi_2-b_2}{\|\nabla\psi_2\|}>0.
\]
Every section has length at most \(D\).  Among all nonnegative section
length functions bounded by \(D\) and having integral \(q_1\), the
first moment is minimized by filling the interval
\([0,q_1/D]\) with density \(D\).  Thus
\[
\int_{Q_1}(\psi_2-b_2)
\geq
\|\nabla\psi_2\|\frac{q_1^2}{2D},
\]
and
\[
\overline\sigma
\geq
\frac{\|\nabla\psi_2\|q_1}{2D}.
\tag{25}
\]
Likewise,
\[
\overline\rho
\geq
\frac{\|\nabla\psi_1\|q_2}{2D}.
\tag{26}
\]
Combining (24)-(26) yields
\[
B_U>
\frac{\eta+g(q_1+q_2)/(2D)}H.
\tag{27}
\]
In particular,
\[
\eta<H B_U,
\qquad
q_1+q_2<\frac{2DH}{g}B_U=A B_U.
\tag{28}
\]
Equations (19), (24), and (28) also prove \(B_U>0\), and they give
\[
B_U>\frac{6d}{H}.
\tag{29}
\]
Passing to (14) proves (15).

We next bound the empty endpoint cell.  The affine map
\[
y\longmapsto(\psi_1(y),\psi_2(y))
\]
has Jacobian magnitude \(J_\psi\).  By (5), the three strict
inequalities defining \(P_\varnothing\) place it inside
\[
\{\psi_1>a_1,\ \psi_2>a_2,\
  \psi_1+\psi_2<-a_3\}.
\]
In the \((\psi_1,\psi_2)\)-plane this is a right triangle with both
legs equal to
\(\delta=-a_1-a_2-a_3\).  Therefore
\[
p_\varnothing
\leq\frac{\delta^2}{2J_\psi}
<\frac{\eta^2}{2J_\psi}
<\frac{H^2}{2J_\psi}B_U^2
=C B_U^2.
\tag{30}
\]

It remains to use the crossings and tails.  From the support (1),
\[
v_1=1-q_2,\qquad
v_2=1-q_1,\qquad
v_3=q_{123}.
\tag{31}
\]
Subtracting the crossing in (2) from its left-tail inequality gives
\[
u_i+v_i\leq1.
\tag{32}
\]
Equations (31)-(32) imply
\[
u_1\leq q_2,\qquad
u_2\leq q_1.
\tag{33}
\]

Every \(P\)-cell other than
\(P_\varnothing\) and \(P_3\) has index \(1\) or \(2\).  Hence
\[
M-p_\varnothing-p_3\leq u_1+u_2.
\tag{34}
\]
Also
\[
p_3\leq u_3\leq1-v_3\leq1
\tag{35}
\]
by (32).  If
\[
\varepsilon=p_\varnothing+q_1+q_2,
\]
then (33)-(35) give
\[
M\leq1+\varepsilon.
\tag{36}
\]
The third crossing and (34) give
\[
h=u_3+v_3+c_3
\geq u_3
\geq p_3
\geq M-\varepsilon
\geq1-\varepsilon.
\tag{37}
\]
On the other hand, (3) and (36) give
\[
h=\frac{2(M+1+k)}9
<\frac{4(M+1)}9
\leq\frac89+\frac{4\varepsilon}{9}.
\tag{38}
\]
Combining (37)-(38) proves
\[
\varepsilon>\frac1{13}.
\tag{39}
\]
Finally, (28) and (30) give
\[
\varepsilon
=p_\varnothing+q_1+q_2
<C B_U^2+A B_U.
\]
Together with (39), this proves (11), and solving the positive
quadratic inequality proves (12).

For completeness, the first-order cap equations in any fixed
low-vertex polygonal stratum are explicit.  If the three bodies and
the normalized affine functions are fixed to first order, put
\[
\ell_{0i}
=\frac{\mathcal H^1(A_0\cap\{\psi_i=a_i\})}
       {\|\nabla\psi_i\|},
\quad
\ell_{2i}
=\frac{\mathcal H^1(A_2\cap\{\psi_i=b_i\})}
       {\|\nabla\psi_i\|},
\]
\[
\ell_{Ki}
=\frac{\mathcal H^1(K\cap\{\psi_i=d\})}
       {\|\nabla\psi_i\|}.
\tag{40}
\]
Differentiating the three crossing equalities on that stratum gives
\[
(\ell_{0i}-\ell_{2i})a_i'
+2\ell_{2i}+\ell_{Ki}=h'
\qquad(i=1,2,3).
\tag{41}
\]
For fixed total areas, \(h'=0\).  If vertices move, the shoelace
derivatives of the three clipped polygons are added to the left side
of (41); no other first-order term occurs.  Thus triangles and
quadrilaterals have only the usual vertex velocities and the three
cut velocities \(a_i'\).  Regardless of how those linear equations
are solved, the exact inequalities (27)-(39) remain valid.  Therefore
no actual low-vertex endpoint realization satisfying all the stated
conditions can have a small finite coefficient \(\beta_U\) with zero
zeroth-order separation.

If, in addition, a finite-stage geometric argument proves
\[
\Delta_3\geq cB_U-Ed
\]
with \(c>0\) and finite \(E\), then (12) gives
\(\Delta_3>0\) for all sufficiently small \(d\), contradicting the
exact third crossing.  This last implication uses the displayed
stability estimate as an additional hypothesis; its proof is outside
the endpoint first-moment calculation established here.
statement:
Assume the affine sign-plane hypotheses, exact-cell convention, and
midpoint compatibility of accepted fact `0e51a47a9add571f`.  Normalize
\[
m=|A_2|=1,\qquad M=|A_0|\geq1,
\]
assume \(p_\varnothing>0\),
and assume the positive \(Q\)-support is exactly
\[
\{123,1,2,12\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Write
\[
q_J=|Q_J|,\qquad p_J=|P_J|,
\]
\[
u_i=\sum_{J\ni i}p_J,\qquad
v_i=\sum_{J\ni i}q_J,\qquad
c_i=\sum_{J\ni i}r_J,
\]
\[
k=|K|,\qquad
h=\frac{2(M+1+k)}9.
\]
Assume all three crossings, the canonical left tails, and the first
no-half inequality:
\[
u_i+v_i+c_i=h,\qquad c_i+1\geq h
\quad(i=1,2,3),
\tag{2}
\]
\[
M<1+k.
\tag{3}
\]

Let \(d>0\), and define normalized affine functions
\[
\psi_i=3d\left(f_i+\frac13\right)
\quad(i=1,2,3).
\tag{4}
\]
Then
\[
\psi_1+\psi_2+\psi_3=0.
\tag{5}
\]
Assume their linear parts are pairwise nonparallel.  Put
\[
J_\psi=
\left|\det(\nabla\psi_1,\nabla\psi_2)\right|>0,
\]
\[
g=\min\{\|\nabla\psi_1\|,\|\nabla\psi_2\|\}>0,
\qquad
H=\|\nabla(\psi_1-\psi_2)\|>0,
\tag{6}
\]
and suppose
\[
\operatorname{diam}(A_2)\leq D.
\tag{7}
\]

Let \(x_\varnothing\) be the area centroid of
\(P_\varnothing\), and let \(y_i\) be the area centroid of \(Q_i\)
for \(i=1,2\).  Define
\[
z_i=\frac{x_\varnothing+y_i}{2}
\in
\frac{P_\varnothing+\overline{Q_i}}2
\subseteq K,
\tag{8}
\]
and define the canonical transverse base
\[
B_U=
\frac{(\psi_1-\psi_2)(z_2)
      -(\psi_1-\psi_2)(z_1)}{H}.
\tag{9}
\]
Then \(B_U>0\), and, with
\[
A=\frac{2DH}{g},
\qquad
C=\frac{H^2}{2J_\psi},
\tag{10}
\]
one has
\[
\boxed{\qquad
C B_U^2+A B_U>\frac1{13}.
\qquad}
\tag{11}
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\boxed{\qquad
B_U>
\frac{\sqrt{A^2+4C/13}-A}{2C}>0.
\qquad}
\tag{12}
\]

For a compact genuine-fan family, uniform upper bounds for \(D,H\)
and \(J_\psi^{-1}\), together with a uniform positive lower bound for
\(g\), turn (12) into a uniform positive modulus.  In the symmetric
standard fan, where the three gradients have unit length and mutual
angle \(120^\circ\),
\[
g=1,\qquad H=\sqrt3,\qquad J_\psi=\frac{\sqrt3}{2},
\]
so (11) becomes
\[
\sqrt3\,B_U^2+2\sqrt3\,D B_U>\frac1{13}.
\tag{13}
\]

Finally, if \(d\downarrow0\), the normalized gradients converge to a
genuine fan, and one nevertheless assumes
\[
B_U(d)=\beta_Ud+o(d),
\tag{14}
\]
then the endpoint offset condition alone implies
\[
\beta_U\geq\frac6{H_0},
\qquad
H_0=\lim_{d\downarrow0}
\|\nabla(\psi_1-\psi_2)\|.
\tag{15}
\]
Under (1)-(3), (12) shows that the expansion (14) cannot occur at all:
the zeroth-order coefficient is already uniformly positive.
